title: H: hydride reservoir re-passivates hammer-aged access transistors in field
idea: Deposit a Pd-capped TiHx hydride strip in the BEOL over each bank, above a window in the SiN hydrogen barrier. A controller-scheduled maintenance pulse from on-die poly heaters (~250 C for seconds, bank taken offline) releases atomic hydrogen that diffuses to the recess-gate Si/SiO2 interface and re-caps dangling bonds created by hot-carrier and hammer stress.
why: Retention tail (fact 3) widens over life as interface traps form; periodic in-field re-passivation keeps weak-cell counts near time-zero, allowing ~2x longer refresh over product life and less test guardband.

title: Li: lithium-ion drift trims threshold of weak access transistors
idea: Embed a LiPON-sealed Li+ pocket in the access-transistor spacer; after wafer-level retention test, a high-field program step drives Li+ away from the channel only on the weakest-leakage transistors, raising their effective Vt ~100 mV, then a low-temperature freeze locks the ions in place.
why: Fixes the <=13 fA leakage tail (fact 3) cell by cell instead of guard-banding the whole array; could move tail-limited refresh from 32 ms toward 128 ms.

title: C: carbon co-implant getters point defects at storage-node junctions
idea: Add a shallow substitutional-carbon co-implant (~1e20 cm^-3) at the storage-node contact junction; carbon traps Si interstitials and binds Fe/Cu, preventing the deep-level clusters that create trap-assisted-tunneling hotspots in the depletion region.
why: Attacks the junction-leakage share of the retention tail (fact 3) with an abundant element already used for diffusion control in logic; target 3-10x fewer tail cells at equal Cs.

title: N: nitride charge-trap sliver as per-row analog hammer dosimeter
idea: A thin SiN charge-trap strip (SONOS-like) under a dummy gate coupled to each wordline receives a small, repeatable charge injection on every activation, so its Vt shift integrates activation count non-volatilely; refresh logic compares it to a threshold, refreshes the neighbors and erases the strip.
why: Row hammer (fact 9) tracking with no SRAM/CAM counter tables, so per-row tracking at ~1k-activation thresholds costs almost no periphery (fact 7).

title: O: oxygen-vacancy recall pulses heal capacitor leakage drift
idea: During refresh-idle windows the array applies brief reverse-polarity, sub-breakdown bias across cell capacitors (plate and bitline swapped) that drifts oxygen vacancies back off the electrode interface, resetting the trap-assisted leakage that grows with time under bias.
why: Makes thinner, higher-k ZrO2/HfO2 stacks (more fF per pillar, fact 1) survive lifetime leakage creep; claim ~2x dielectric lifetime or ~15% more Cs at the same lifetime.

title: F: fluorine-hardened recess-gate edge resists hot-carrier depassivation
idea: A tilted low-dose fluorine implant aimed only at the gate-to-storage-node overlap corner replaces Si-H with Si-F bonds (~5.7 eV vs ~3.1 eV), so hammer-induced hot carriers and GIDL fields cannot re-create the interface traps behind RTN and variable retention time.
why: Cuts VRT cells and lifetime growth of the leakage tail (fact 3) plus trap-assisted hammer coupling (fact 9); target ~2x fewer VRT cells.

title: Na: sodium-dosed sentinel capacitors forecast mat failure early
idea: Each mat carries a few SiN-encapsulated sentinel cells whose dielectric holds a controlled Na+ dose, so they leak and age ~10x faster under identical temperature and voltage; refresh logic polls them and tightens refresh or retires the mat as soon as sentinels start failing.
why: Turns retention-tail uncertainty (fact 3) into a measured early warning, so nominal refresh can run with less guardband (~1.5-2x longer tREFI) without risking silent errors.

title: Mg: MgO stochastic tunnel junctions as coin-flip hammer counters
idea: A BEOL MgO magnetic tunnel junction beside each row driver gets a sub-critical pulse on every activation, switching with probability ~1/500 from thermal noise; a switched junction triggers neighbor refresh and is reset, giving a hardware probabilistic counter with no tables and no attacker-predictable state.
why: Row hammer (fact 9) protection below 1k-activation thresholds with near-zero periphery area (fact 7) and true randomness for free.

title: Al: Al2O3 negative charge passivates storage junction surfaces, solar-style
idea: Line STI sidewalls and the buried-wordline trench top near the storage node with ALD Al2O3, whose ~-5e12 cm^-2 fixed negative charge accumulates holes at the p-type surface and pushes the depletion region off the defective interface (the field-effect passivation used in PERC solar cells).
why: Suppresses surface-generation leakage, a major retention-tail contributor (fact 3), with abundant Al and existing ALD; target 2-5x tail reduction.

title: Si: silicon-on-nothing voids block substrate electron migration between rows
idea: Form empty-space-in-silicon cavities (trench array plus hydrogen-anneal surface migration) under the storage-node regions so electrons released during aggressor wordline cycling cannot diffuse through the substrate to neighbor storage nodes, while junction volume (generation leakage) shrinks.
why: Cuts the charge-migration row-hammer path (fact 9) and the junction-leakage tail (fact 3); could raise the hammer threshold ~10x.

title: P: buried phosphorus collector line sweeps hammer-injected electrons away
idea: A deep n+ phosphorus stripe runs between adjacent rows under the passing wordline, biased slightly positive, acting as a drain that collects electrons emitted from traps when aggressor wordlines toggle, before they reach victim storage nodes.
why: Device-level row hammer (fact 9) mitigation that needs no counters or extra refresh; claim ~5-10x higher first-flip activation count.

title: S: sulfide threshold switch adds a leakage dead zone per cell
idea: Insert a GeS-based ovonic threshold switch (sulfur chalcogenide, As- and Se-free) between the access transistor and the capacitor; small leakage-driven voltage drops sit inside its hold-voltage dead zone and cannot drain the node, while full read/write pulses exceed threshold.
why: Decouples retention and disturb immunity from the access-transistor leakage tail (fact 3) and passing-gate disturb (fact 9); speculative but could remove most refresh.

title: Ca: CaF2 crystalline gate insulator removes RTN traps from access devices
idea: Grow lattice-matched crystalline CaF2 on (111)-faceted recess sidewalls as the access-transistor gate insulator; a crystalline fluoride has far fewer border traps than amorphous SiO2/HfO2, eliminating the single-trap telegraph switching behind variable retention time.
why: VRT cells force multi-pass retention profiling and extra refresh margin (fact 3); removing them could cut VRT cells ~10x and simplify refresh binning.

title: Ti: titanium getter ring in hybrid-bond seal absorbs moisture
idea: Pattern a Ti/Zr getter line inside the hybrid-bonding seal ring of each stacked DRAM die so moisture and stray hydrogen entering through dicing edges are chemisorbed before reaching TSV liners and capacitor dielectrics.
why: Prevents time-dependent leakage drift and TSV corrosion in stacks, lifting HBM yield and field life (fact 6) with an abundant, MEMS-proven getter.

title: V: VO2 phase-change thermal integrator flags hammered subarrays
idea: A doped VO2 sliver (insulator-metal transition tuned near 70 C) is thermally coupled to each subarray's local wordline driver; sustained high activation rates heat it through the transition, its resistance drop trips a sense line that forces targeted neighbor refresh, while normal traffic never heats it enough.
why: Analog, counter-free hammer-rate detection (fact 9) that costs no logic area; complements fine-grained trackers.

title: Zn: indium-free zinc-tin-oxide TFT layer hosts ECC logic above array
idea: Fabricate a BEOL ZnSnO thin-film-transistor logic layer (Zn and Sn are abundant; no In or Ga) over the cell array to hold on-die ECC syndrome decoders and row/column repair muxes, wired down by vias to local sense amps.
why: Moves reliability logic out of the ~49% periphery (fact 7) so stronger on-die ECC costs no die area; ~3-5% die shrink or 2x ECC strength at equal area.

title: Sn: tin-bismuth microbumps self-reflow to heal opened HBM joints
idea: Use low-melting Sn-Bi (~139 C) microbumps with resistive heaters on the base die; when built-in self-test finds an open or high-resistance joint, the controller pulses local heat to re-melt and re-wet it, with spare TSV lanes as fallback.
why: HBM stack yield loss of 20-30% (fact 6) and field joint opens; recovering half the open-joint fallout adds ~10% usable HBM supply.

title: Ce: ceria oxygen-storage interlayer self-heals capacitor dielectric vacancies
idea: Insert ~1 nm CeO2 between the TiN electrode and ZrO2 dielectric; ceria cycles Ce3+/Ce4+ as in automotive catalytic converters, absorbing oxygen vacancies and releasing oxygen to buffer the vacancy profile that drives leakage drift and breakdown.
why: Lets capacitors run thinner, higher-capacitance dielectrics (fact 1) without lifetime leakage creep; target ~2x higher allowed field.

title: Ar: argon-implanted recombination layer annihilates stray carriers below cells
idea: Implant argon deep below the active cell region to form a thin damaged layer with short minority-carrier lifetime (the IGBT lifetime-control trick), placed outside junction depletion regions, so substrate electrons recombine before diffusing to storage nodes.
why: Cuts substrate-mediated row hammer (fact 9) and alpha/neutron charge collection; claim ~3x lower soft-error rate, letting weaker Cs pass.

title: Cu: copper conductive-bridge antifuses give unlimited in-field row remapping
idea: Replace one-time fuses in the repair block with Cu-ion conductive-bridge cells programmable at ~1.5 V in the field, so the controller can remap hundreds of failing rows and columns over life (and undo them), instead of DDR5's handful of post-package-repair slots.
why: Self-healing repair makes weaker arrays acceptable: less test guardband, higher yield and fewer DIMM replacements.

title: Mo: grounded molybdenum shield fins screen buried-wordline passing-gate coupling
idea: Insert a thin grounded Mo fin between adjacent buried wordlines, electrostatically screening the passing-gate field that modulates neighbor channels and storage-node junctions; Mo also replaces some tungsten (an 80%-China chokepoint) and is mined in the U.S.
why: Attacks the passing-gate row-hammer mechanism (fact 9) and GIDL tail (fact 3) at the source; target 5x higher hammer threshold.

title: Ge: germanium strike-detector diodes turn soft errors into cheap erasures
idea: A grid of SiGe particle-strike detector diodes under each mat timestamps and localizes ion strikes; the controller marks the affected symbols as erasures, and because a code corrects twice as many erasures as unknown errors, the same ECC budget covers double the failure density.
why: Keeps on-die ECC overhead low (~6% die) while tolerating smaller Cs and weaker cells; also guides targeted scrubbing.

title: Si: retention-graded silicon sells dies failing 64 ms as R-grade
idea: Create a JEDEC-style relaxed-retention grade (e.g., 16 ms refresh window) with a per-die weak-row map written into SPD; host controllers refresh faster only where flagged, and AI-inference fleets buy these dies at a discount.
why: Recovers dies now scrapped or down-binned for retention tails (est. 3-8% of output), raising usable supply during the 4x price spike.

title: B: boron-10 hBN coating shields DIMMs from thermal neutrons
idea: A small coating line sprays an epoxy loaded with 10B-enriched hexagonal boron nitride flakes over DRAM packages on DIMMs and HBM modules; 10B absorbs thermal neutrons before they reach residual 10B in die dielectrics, and hBN spreads heat. Needs only mixing, a spray booth and a cure oven.
why: Cuts the thermal-neutron share of soft errors (large near concrete and water-rich datacenters), letting operators relax scrub rate or ECC strength.

title: Cu: copper cold-plate DIMM sleeves buy 4x longer refresh
idea: A machined, brazed copper sleeve plumbed into the server's existing liquid loop holds DRAM packages below 45 C; after a per-module retention screen, BIOS tables set tREFI 2-4x longer. CNC and brazing fit a 10-person shop.
why: Retention roughly doubles per 10 C; recovers much of the 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth lost to refresh (fact 3).

title: N: liquid-nitrogen memory sled where refresh nearly disappears
idea: A small team builds a dewar-cooled, CXL-attached 1U memory sled running commodity DDR5 at ~77-120 K, where junction leakage freezes out so retention stretches to seconds and refresh is throttled ~100x; an FPGA controller re-tunes timings.
why: Eliminates the refresh tax and leakage-tail errors (fact 3) using off-the-shelf DRAM; cryocooler power is partly offset by lower wire resistance.

title: Na: rock-salt lattice data inversion picks least-hammerable neighbor pattern
idea: Like Na+ and Cl- alternating in a crystal, controller RTL XORs data with a physical-row-parity mask (learned from the DIMM's address scramble) chosen per module after profiling which neighbor charge relation (same or opposite) flips least, so adjacent rows mostly hold the benign pattern. FPGA/RTL only.
why: Row hammer flips (fact 9) are strongly data-pattern dependent; enforcing the benign relation claims ~2-5x higher effective threshold.

title: Zn: zinc sacrificial-anode rows absorb hammer flips beside hot rows
idea: Like zinc galvanizing steel, the OS page allocator and controller place only recomputable content (clean page-cache copies, parity, prefetch buffers) in rows physically adjacent to detected hot rows, so flips land where they are harmless and heal on re-fetch. Software plus firmware.
why: Turns row hammer (fact 9) from a correctness failure into a small cache-miss cost with no new hardware.

title: Ca: bone-remodeling scrubber resorbs and rebuilds rows by stress
idea: Controller firmware runs osteoclast/osteoblast loops: scrub rate per region scales with its access stress (Wolff's law), rows whose corrected-error rate climbs are resorbed (data migrated, row retired via PPR or OS page offlining) and spare capacity is rebuilt.
why: Self-healing lets weaker DIMMs serve full lives; targets ~10x fewer uncorrectable errors than fixed-rate scrub at equal scrub bandwidth.

title: Fe: iron-boron pair photodissociation screen bins wafers for retention
idea: A benchtop laser plus photoconductance tool measures minority-carrier lifetime before and after a flash that splits Fe-B pairs, giving interstitial iron per wafer; a 10-person company sells it as incoming-wafer screening that routes iron-rich wafers away from retention-critical products.
why: Iron is a top retention-tail culprit (fact 3); early binning lifts yield and lets fabs qualify wafers grown in non-Spruce-Pine crucibles safely.

title: Si: silicone microcapsule underfill self-heals cracks in memory stacks
idea: Formulate an underfill with PDMS healing-agent microcapsules and a tin catalyst (no platinum); a growing microcrack ruptures capsules and seals itself before moisture and stress concentrate on microbumps. A small formulation and dispensing line suffices.
why: Thermal-cycle cracking drives opens in HBM/3DS stacks (fact 6); target ~2x thermal-cycle life.

title: Al: self-passivating pages escalate ECC in place like alumina
idea: Like aluminum growing oxide only where exposed, controller RTL escalates a page to a stronger mode (extra symbols borrowed from a metadata carve-out, or duplicate plus checksum) the moment it logs a correctable error, leaving the rest of memory at lean ECC.
why: Spends ECC overhead only on weak cells, keeping average overhead ~12.5% while approaching strong-ECC reliability, which makes weaker DIMMs acceptable.

title: Ba: barium-titanate acoustic sensors catch stack microcracks early
idea: Bond lead-free BaTiO3 piezo acoustic-emission sensors to HBM/3DS package lids; firmware listens for crack-burst signatures during thermal cycles and pre-emptively migrates data off the affected die and channel before joints open. Off-the-shelf piezo plus a small DSP board.
why: Converts sudden stack failures (fact 6) into planned remaps, cutting uncorrectable events and allowing cheaper, less-qualified stacks.

title: C: graphene-hex interleave spreads clustered flips across codewords
idea: Map codeword bits onto physical columns and chips in a honeycomb pattern, so bits that are physical neighbors (which fail together from shared defects or hammer hot zones) always fall in different codewords, each seeing at most one bad symbol. A remap table in controller RTL.
why: Turns clustered multi-bit failures (facts 8-9) into single-symbol errors that existing SEC or chipkill corrects; claim ~10x fewer uncorrectable events.

title: S: vulcanized cross-channel parity rebuilds rows lost to hammer
idea: Like sulfur cross-linking rubber chains, a CXL/FPGA controller keeps the XOR of row N across four channels in a fifth channel, updated on writeback, so a row that on-die ECC reports uncorrectable is rebuilt from the cross-link.
why: Chipkill cannot fix whole-row or multi-chip loss; ~25% capacity overhead buys tolerance of hammer wipeouts and dead dies, enabling cheaper DIMMs.

title: Ga: gallium-tin liquid-metal contacts self-heal intermittent DIMM connectors
idea: An interposer with sealed microcups of Ga-Sn eutectic (In-free; gram quantities despite gallium's China concentration) replaces spring contacts; the liquid metal flows around fretting and oxide, eliminating intermittent connector faults that masquerade as memory errors and trigger DIMM pulls.
why: Many field 'memory failures' are connector or signal-integrity faults; avoiding needless replacement raises effective supply.

title: K: potassium-40 half-life tags skip refresh for short-lived data
idea: Allocator APIs tag buffers with an expected lifetime, like a radioisotope half-life; the controller tracks per-row last-write time and suppresses refresh for rows whose data will be rewritten or freed before retention expires (activations, KV caches, DMA buffers).
why: Cuts refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) in AI training memory, where most data lives under 64 ms.

title: Au: gold rows hold critical data in best-retention cells
idea: Boot-time firmware profiling ranks rows into gold, silver and bronze retention bins; the hypervisor maps kernel, page tables and model weights to gold rows at relaxed refresh and puts streaming and cache data in bronze rows with faster refresh.
why: Matches data criticality to cell quality instead of uniform worst-case refresh; ~30-50% refresh reduction (fact 3).

title: Fe: let the mantissa rust while exponent bits stay protected
idea: Like a thick iron beam that tolerates surface rust, a model-loading library splits bf16/fp8 weights so sign and exponent bits live in ECC-protected, normally refreshed rows while low mantissa bits sit in rows with 4x relaxed refresh and no ECC.
why: Neural nets tolerate mantissa flips, so ~60% of weight bits get cheaper storage and refresh, letting weaker cells serve inference.

title: Mg: polymerase-style proofreading verifies writes before row close
idea: Like DNA polymerase's Mg2+-dependent proofreading, controller RTL reads back freshly written columns before precharge while the row is still open and checks ECC; a mismatch triggers a rewrite with longer tWR or a remap.
why: Write-recovery failures grow as Cs shrinks (fact 1); verifying catches them before they become latent errors and allows aggressive tWR safely.

title: Sn: tin-can preservation compresses cold pages to fund ECC
idea: The controller compresses cold pages (typically 1.5-2x) and fills the freed bits with a strong Reed-Solomon code in place, so these pages tolerate 8-16x relaxed refresh in a low-refresh region with no capacity loss. Firmware plus RTL.
why: Cuts refresh energy (fact 3) for the cold majority of memory and makes weak cells tolerable.

title: Li: lithium-6 rack neutron monitor drives space-weather scrubbing
idea: A 6Li-glass scintillator neutron counter per row of racks (no scarce He-3), plus public neutron-monitor feeds, lets the fleet raise scrub rates and ECC modes during solar particle events or at high-altitude sites and relax them otherwise.
why: Soft-error rate tracks neutron flux (~2x over the solar cycle, several x with altitude), so the fleet stops paying worst-case scrub energy all year.

title: Si: mature-node hammer-guard buffer chip for commodity DIMMs
idea: A 10-person fabless team tapes out a small 28-40 nm companion chip on a multi-project wafer that sits beside the RCD, snoops ACT commands, keeps Misra-Gries hot-row counters and issues targeted refresh-management commands to any vendor's DRAM.
why: Retrofits strong row hammer protection (fact 9) onto cheaper DRAM using U.S.-manufacturable mature-node silicon.

title: O: lambda-sensor loop tunes DDR5 PMIC voltages to error rate
idea: Like an engine O2 sensor trimming fuel, DIMM firmware closes a loop on corrected-error and hammer-alert rates and nudges the on-DIMM PMIC's VPP and VDD within spec, lowering VPP to reduce hammer susceptibility and raising it if retention errors climb.
why: Finds each module's reliable minimum-energy point, cutting wordline CV2 energy (fact 10) and hammer flips (fact 9) using existing I2C-programmable PMICs.

title: U: enrichment-cascade grading of secondhand DRAM for matched workloads
idea: Like centrifuge cascades enriching U-235, a line of FPGA testers in series progressively sorts used DIMMs by retention, hammer threshold and error history into grades, each sold with a workload certificate (error-tolerant AI cache, general compute, critical).
why: Recovers decommissioned modules into usable supply during the 4x price spike with minimal capital.

title: Ti: titanium-airframe damage tolerance schedules DIMM replacement from error growth
idea: Borrowing aerospace titanium inspection logic (Paris-law crack growth), fleet software fits each DIMM's correctable-error growth curve and predicts time to first uncorrectable error, scheduling replacement or regrading at planned maintenance.
why: Keeps weaker modules safely in service longer and avoids crashes; cuts premature replacements ~30%.
